Title: Defence Marine Services - Supply and Maintenance of Authority Moorings, Markers and Targets - AC
Description:
The Contract covers the following services: the maintenance of moorings, target moorings and navigation marks owned by the Authority, the replacement of moorings and navigation marks with telemetry buoys and the sourcing, storage and supply of moorings and navigation mark components.
The maintenance and replacement of moorings, target moorings and navigation marks service will be provided at various locations around the UK Coast including Gibraltar and Cyprus. The supply of moorings and navigation mark components to a UK based nominated point of departure to enable the Authority to transport to the Ascension Island and Falkland Islands.

To facilitate service delivery the intent is to transfer ownership of an Authority owned vessel to the new service provider under a Contractor Owned Contractor Operated (COCO) agreement subject to equitable financial renumeration. This vessel and any other vessel operated under this contract shall be UK Flagged and Certified.
The specification for the services will include the following:
- Maintenance in accordance with the Mooring Maintenance Programme (MMP), a schedule of routine mooring and navigation mark maintenance to ensure moorings and navigation marks remain safe to operate.
- A Moorings Replacement Programme (MRP) to replace moorings and navigation marks with telemetry buoys. The MRP will involve the total removal of the legacy mooring, the design and assurance of the new moorings, the procurement of replacement components and the installation and assurance of the new moorings.
- The sourcing, storage, and delivery of components to an authority nominated UK point of departure, allowing the Authority to maintain moorings in Ascension Island and Falkland Islands.

Title: Digital Decision Accelerators for Defence (DDAD), UK6 Contract Award Notification (CAN)
Description:
The Ministry of Defence (MOD) has concluded its procurement process for a new Defence and Security Open Framework, specifically created to foster a deep eco-system for advanced digital decision-supporting capabilities. An Open Framework is a scheme of successive framework iterations that are periodically re-opened (competed) under substantially unchanged terms.

For the avoidance of doubt within this published CAN, as an Open Framework the listed Suppliers are subject to change following a framework reopening. When this occurs, the Authority will communicate this update with industry via updating this notice or issuing a new one with an updated Framework Member list. 

This Open Framework will serve as the primary delivery route for ASGARD; the British Army's flagship Transformative Capability Initiative (TCI). ASGARD forms a central componennt of the Chief of the General Staff's Growth Through Transformation (GTT) Strategy. The DDAD Framework may be used as agreed to procure other, non-ASGARD, goods and services.

The Framework will operate for an initial four (4) core year period, with optional extensions detailed elsewhere. 

The maximum throughput of the framework during the 'Core' period is £180,000,000 (Ex. VAT). This figure represents a ceiling ("Headroom") of spend rather than any spending commitment. 

The MOD has carefully considered its approach to 'lots', and detailed of SME considerations were issued in previous publications. The Structure and process was designed to be accessible, and this has been successful in that 50% of suppliers (14 out of 26) are UK- based SMEs.

In total, twenty-six (26) suppliers were successful. Six (6) of these Suppliers secured placed on two (2) lots - the maximum allowed.

Title: Submarine Escape and Survival Equipment (SESE) Contract Award Notice
Description:
The purpose of Submarine Escape and Survival Equipment (SESE) is to allow submariners to evacuate from a disabled submerged submarine, without external assistance, in a safe and controlled manner. The intention of the equipment is to keep the escapee dry and protected from the environment during and after ascent, and to provide buoyancy, freeboard, and thermal insulation at the surface.

The SESE is a whole-body suit comprising a one-size fits all Submarine Escape Survival Suit (SESS) and a Single person life raft all contained in a protective valise.

A competitive procurement has been conducted for supply of 3884 operational SESE and 120 training variant SESE and ad hoc repairs of training variant SESE on a tasking basis.

Equipment

Activities that support this capability include, but are not limited to; Asset Transition from current location, Responsibility as Design Organisation, Asset Management including receipt and issue of demands for equipment, Management of Equipment Safety, Post Design Services, Through Life Support including maintenance, repair and supply of spares, User Single Point of Contact, Provision and Update of Technical Documentation, Obsolescence Management, with the possibility of Training provision.

The Contractor will be required to work with an incumbent provider (Babcock) who is responsible for the provision of Level 2-3 Maintenance for all Standard variant FEPS equipment under the Service Provision and Transformation Contract (SPTC).

The fleet of equipment will be held at various readiness levels to meet operational planning assumptions.

Title: Project BRACIS
Description:
The Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Delivery Team (CBRN DT) within the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) has extended a single source Contract with Bruhn Newtech Ltd (BNT Ltd) for the support of Biological, Radiological and Chemical (BRaCIS) Warning and Reporting (W&R) software for a period of 4 years to FY 2030 with 1 x option year until 2031 to provide a continuing requirement to support the In-Service CBRN W&R software including training for UK Defence. 
A VTN was published for transparency purposes. 
It is considered that this extension to contract can be awarded using the negotiated procedure without prior publication of a contract notice, pursuant to Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the UK Defence and Security Public Contract Regulations 2011 (No 1848), for technical reasons. BRaCIS software is owned, designed and maintained by BNT Ltd, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). Despite the W&R software being a Commercial of The Shelf (COTS) item used by additional NATO countries, this software with BNT Ltd has been modified to meet the UK bespoke requirements defined by the UK MOD. These modifications are essential to make it compatible with the UK Defence BOWMAN ComBAT Information Platform (BCiP), operating on the BCiP networking platform. Title: Provision of Furniture at Catterick Integrated Care Centre (CICC)
Description:
1. The purpose of this procurement is to purchase furniture to support the opening of CICC on 1st September 2026.

2. A thorough condition assessment of the existing furniture in the current healthcare facilities was conducted by the Facilities Officer, who concluded that most items have exceeded their serviceable life. The furniture is no longer fit for purpose, cannot be safely dismantled or moved to the new facility, and presents potential health and safety hazards due to structural deterioration resulting in failure to meet current standards.

3. Furthermore, the new healthcare facility will offer increased capacity, including additional clinical areas, office spaces, staff rest rooms, meeting rooms, and a larger waiting area for Medical, Dental, and Department of Community Mental Health (DCMH) patients. This expansion results in a significant shortfall of appropriate furnishings and fittings, requiring the purchase of new DAS-compliant items to ensure full operational readiness for the planned move-in date of 1st September 2026.

4. The CICC is a joint MOD/NHS facility incorporating patient wayfinding, divided into four colour-coded zones. During the design phase, it was agreed that the waiting area furniture would correspond with these wayfinding colours. Tilbury Douglas (CICC Delivery Partner) will install custom-built furniture in these zones as part of the Group 1 items. The remaining waiting area furniture is classified as Group 3 items, which the Authority shall procure and to which this requirement pertains.

5. The Authority requires Group 3 Waiting Area furniture. This is broken down into both CORE and NON-CORE items.

6. All Group 3 Waiting Area furniture items must be wipeable, vinyl covered and meet Infection Prevention Control standards in accordance with Para 5.36.1.2 - NHS - Infection Control, of RM6308 Framework Schedule 1 - Specification.

7. The Authority requires the Contractor to deliver and instal all Group 3 Waiting Area furniture in the designated areas per the Scoping Plan by 1st September 2026 at the latest.

8. The Authority requires office furniture. This is broken down into both CORE and NON-CORE items.

9. Office furniture items that are listed as wipeable must be vinyl covered and meet Infection Prevention Control standards in accordance with Para 5.36.1.2 - NHS - Infection Control, of RM6308 Framework Schedule 1 - Specification.

10. The Authority requires the Contractor to deliver and instal all office furniture in the designated areas per the Scoping Plan by 8th September 2026 at the latest.

11. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of all packaging in accordance with good industry practice.

12. Please include any training or skills transfer requirements to be delivered by the Supplier.
